📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Omari Hutchinson has spoken about his preferred role, while praising the AC Milan fans and revealing his belief the Scudetto is a realistic target.

According to recent reports, hutchinson joined Milan on an initial loan deal from Nottingham Forest with an option to buy. He scored his first goal for the club in the away win over Udinese last month, and is getting more regular minutes on the right side.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that in fact, the head coach Ruben Amorim has even deployed him as a wing-back on occasion. Given the injuries to Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze the Englishman’s role has become an even more vital one than first imagined.

Hutchinson met with fans this afternoon at the Milan Store in San Babila in the city centre. While at the event, the winger gave an interview to the reporters who were present, with MilanNews relaying his words.

Recent findings suggest that how have these first few months at Milan been? Are you raising your game?

“It’s going well, the coach is happy, but I think there’s still a lot to do. I’m earning myself some space… From here on out, we have to keep winning.”.

We often see you on the wing. Do you prefer to play there or as a second striker?

“Personally, I like to play anywhere, but preferably on the right flank. Then, wherever the coach puts me, I try to adapt, do my job, and perform to my best, following his tactical instructions. He knows what I can do with the ball. He simply tells me to create and give my all.”.

How is your relationship with Amorim?

“He talks to me about what to do with the ball and to do my best.”.

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

“It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”.

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

“Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”.

Do you think Milan can win the Scudetto?

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”.

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

“It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”.

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

“It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”.

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

In a recent development, “They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

Industry observers note that “In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that significant a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”.

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

It has been revealed that “No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”.

Do you dream of making the national team?

“I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 15:50, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:53.
  • Rayo Vallecano and Valencia will both be looking to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume their respective La Liga campaigns in Madrid on Saturday.
  • Valencia's last match at this level ended in a 3-0 reverse to Real Madrid, while Rayo were beaten 1-0 by Real Sociedad in their final fixture ahead of the November international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 15:50, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:53.

Rayo Vallecano and Valencia will both be looking to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume their respective La Liga campaigns in Madrid on Saturday.

Valencia's last match at this level ended in a 3-0 reverse to Real Madrid, while Rayo were beaten 1-0 by Real Sociedad in their final fixture ahead of the November international break.

Rayo have a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with a total of 12 points leaving them in 14th spot in the La Liga table.

The capital outfit are currently six points off sixth-placed Sevilla and two points outside of the relegation zone, so it has been a mixed start to the campaign, and they have only managed to win one of their last five fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Benat San Jose's side have been impressive on home soil this season, picking up 10 points from five matches, but it has been a struggle for them on their travels, yet to record a win from six fixtures.

Los Franjirrojos, who finished eighth in Spain's top flight last season, have only managed to win 10 of their previous 52 matches against Valencia throughout history.

However, four of their last five contests have finished all square, including a 1-1 draw in the corresponding match between the two teams last season.

Valencia have not actually beaten Rayo since December 2023, while they have just two wins over the capital outfit in all competitions since December 2014.

Seven of the last 10 matches between these two teams have finished level, but Los Che will have their eyes on what would be just a third league win of the campaign.

A record of two wins, three draws and seven defeats from 12 matches has left Javier Aguirre's side down in 19th spot in the table, picking up just nine points.

Los Che suffered a 3-0 defeat to Real Madrid in their last league fixture, but they have been in action since, securing their spot in the second round of the Copa del Rey courtesy of a 6-0 victory over Tavernes on November 10.

Valencia have actually claimed seven of their nine league points this season on their travels, boasting a record of two wins, one draw and two defeats.

Rayo Vallecano form (all competitions):.

Valencia form (all competitions):.

Rayo will again be missing Augusto Batalla through injury this weekend, while Alvaro Garcia, Marash Kumbulla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin could also be absent.

Sergio Camello has scored seven times in 12 league appearances during the 2026-27 campaign, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There is also set to be a spot in the wide for Jorge de Frutos, while Pathe Ciss should continue in the middle of the midfield for the capital outfit.

As for Valencia, Jose Gaya is suspended following his red card against Real Madrid.

Sergi Canos is a long-term absentee due to a serious knee injury, while Diego Lopez and David Otorbi remain fitness doubts for the away side.

Umar Sadiq and Arnaut Danjuma are facing late fitness tests, but the expectation is that the duo will be available for selection on Saturday.

There will be changes to the side that started the game against Real Madrid, with Luis Rioja and Filip Ugrinic expected to be introduced into the XI.

Rayo Vallecano possible starting lineup:.

Audero; Ratiu, Lejeune, Sadick, Pedrosa; Lopez, Ciss; De Frutos, Diaz, Palazon; Camello.

Valencia possible starting lineup:.

Dimitrievski; Maffeo, Pepelu, Tarrega, De Haas; Guerra, Rodriguez, Ugrinic; Danjuma, Sadiq, Rioja.

Recent history points to a draw on Saturday, with the two teams sharing the spoils on a number of occasions of late; a close match could potentially finish 1-1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:49 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 15 November 2026.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

Bacher, 30, essentially failed to let go of the ball at the right time, leaving his team-mates stunned.

The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

It has been revealed that arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

"Están matando al fútbol"Por el "insólito" gol en contra que se hace el arquero de Comunicaciones ante Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/GLUJlcKPXK.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored a bizarre own goal during his side's third-tier play-off game.

The 30-year-old failed to release the ball from a throw and released the ball into his own net.

Fans flooded to social media to react to the scarcely believable own goal.

One wrote on X: 'Haha, those who think it's because of betting. That's the level of Argentine football.'.

Another posted: 'RIP Argentinian football.'.

Industry observers note that A third shared: 'The Arsenal lot celebrating... you've got some nerve.'.

Bacher joined the club at the start of last year, but has always played in his homeland of Argentina.

His Comunicaciones side finished ninth in their league group of Primera B, the third tier of Argentinian football, and were taken on by an Arsenal side that came second.

They will face off in the return leg next Saturday.

Southampton vs Derby County - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (667 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 15:52, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:54.
  • Southampton will resume their Championship campaign with a home clash against Derby County on Saturday.
  • The Saints return from the international break in seventh spot, while the Rams are languishing in 23rd place in the Championship table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 15:52, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:54.

Southampton will resume their Championship campaign with a home clash against Derby County on Saturday.

The Saints return from the international break in seventh spot, while the Rams are languishing in 23rd place in the Championship table.

Southampton enjoyed a fine run of form after returning from the September/October international break, recording four wins and two draws in a six-game unbeaten run.

However, their undefeated streak came to a disappointing end with a 1-0 away loss against basement side Preston North End in their final outing before the two-week break.

Tonda Eckert’s side failed to produce a response to Jordan Thompson’s 33rd-minute effort, as they drew a blank for the first time on the road this season.

Despite that result, the Saints are still firmly in the promotion battle, sitting in seventh spot and five points adrift of the automatic promotion places ahead of Saturday’s meeting with the Rams.

They head into that contest with the league’s best home record, having won six and drawn one of their seven Championship outings at St Mary’s this term, scoring 20 goals and conceding on just five occasions.

They have also won their last two home league games against Derby, including a hard-fought 2-1 victory in April’s encounter between the two sides.

While the Saints are targeting promotion, Derby are focusing on retaining their Championship status after winning just two of their 15 league matches (D4, L9).

They at least managed to end a 10-game winless run in their final outing before the international window, which saw them overturn a one-goal deficit to record a 3-1 victory over Bolton Wanderers.

Ryan Nyambe, Jack Robinson and Rhian Brewster all found the net in the second period to ease some of the heavy pressure on head coach John Eustace.

However, Eustace knows he needs a positive run of results if he is to prove he is the right manager to lead Derby out of their current predicament, with five points separating the Rams from safety.

Derby have failed to win any of their last five away games, but they have at least enjoyed success on the south coast this season, with September’s 2-0 win over Portsmouth representing their only win on the road this term.

If they are to claim the spoils on Saturday, the visitors will need to claim their first Championship win at St Mary’s since recording a 2-1 victory in the second leg of the 2006-07 playoff semi-finals.

Derby County Championship form:.

Southampton defender Keven Schlotterbeck will be out for around six weeks after suffering a dislocated shoulder in the defeat to Preston.

The Saints will also have to assess their star forward Cyle Larin, who missed the last four games before the international window with a hamstring problem.

Midfielder Caspar Jander is another injury concern, having sat out the previous three matches with a muscular injury.

As for the Rams, Sammie Szmodics is expected to be out until mid-December after sustaining a knee injury in the loss to Norwich at the start of the month.

Derby are also without Craig Forsyth, Sondre Langas, Charlie Taylor and Derry Murkin for the trip to the south coast.

Eiran Cashin, Matt Clarke, Joe Ward, Ryan Hedges and Patrick Agyemang are closing in on making their respective returns from injury, although it remains to be seen whether any of the quintet will be ready for Saturday’s fixture.

Southampton possible starting lineup:.

Peretz; Bree, Stephens, Abbott, Manning; Downes, Ward-Prowse; Matsuki, Azaz, Scienza; Dobbin.

Derby County possible starting lineup:.

Widell Zetterstrom; Nyambe, Duffy, Sanderson, Robinson; Travis, Ozoh; Brewster, Clark, Fuseini; Morris.

Southampton have dropped just two points across their first seven home league games, and we think they will enjoy another victorious outing in front of their supporters, considering Derby have lost three of their last five away trips.

#2149. Industry News: Middlesbrough vs Bristol City - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1101 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Middlesbrough vs Bristol City - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 15:53, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:00.
  • Middlesbrough will be looking to move to the top of the Championship table this weekend when they welcome a struggling Bristol City side to the Riverside Stadium.
  • Boro entered the final international break of the year having missed the opportunity to become league leaders, as a defeat to Wrexham was followed by a goalless draw away to Watford, while the Robins continued their slide down the table after suffering a humiliating 5-0 home defeat to Norwich City just under a fortnight ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 15:53, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:00.

Middlesbrough will be looking to move to the top of the Championship table this weekend when they welcome a struggling Bristol City side to the Riverside Stadium.

Boro entered the final international break of the year having missed the opportunity to become league leaders, as a defeat to Wrexham was followed by a goalless draw away to Watford, while the Robins continued their slide down the table after suffering a humiliating 5-0 home defeat to Norwich City just under a fortnight ago.

Kim Hellberg and his Middlesbrough side return to the Riverside Stadium for the first time since Halloween with an opportunity to leapfrog Birmingham City and move to the top of the Championship table.

The Blues have made an unexpected push for first place in recent weeks after winning three consecutive matches, while Boro managed just one victory, alongside a defeat and a draw, leaving both sides level on 29 points ahead of matchweek 16.

Such is the competitiveness of the Championship that Middlesbrough's tally of 29 points provides them with just a three-point cushion over sixth place, highlighting how rapidly the standings can change.

Although their form at the start of November was somewhat inconsistent, Boro return to home soil where they are unbeaten in seven matches, collecting 17 points and scoring 17 goals during that run, with only Southampton boasting a better home record than Hellberg's side.

Last season saw Hellberg and his Middlesbrough team miss out on promotion to the Premier League following one of the most dramatic and controversial playoff campaigns in recent memory, despite occupying a place in the top two for much of the season.

Their success during the 2025-26 campaign was built on a prolific attack that scored 72 goals in 46 matches, a total bettered by just three teams, and they have once again impressed in the final third this season, with only one side scoring more than their 30 goals.

As for Bristol City, they entered the international break with serious questions surrounding the future of manager Michael Skubala after a dreadful run of form saw them fall out of the playoff places and down to 17th in the table.

Since the first international break ended in September, the Robins have won just one of their subsequent seven Championship matches and were widely tipped to part manufacturer with the former Lincoln City boss during the past fortnight, but the club have opted to stick with him as he prepares to take charge of his 17th match on Saturday.

A short video published by the club last week showed CEO Charlie Boss confirming that they would "give Skubala the opportunity to turn around the home form", with Bristol City's two victories at Ashton Gate representing the fourth-worst record in the division and a stark contrast to that of their upcoming opponents.

The Robins enjoyed a productive seven-day spell in which they collected nine points from a possible nine against Portsmouth, Preston North End and Burnley, but have since suffered a series of disappointing results that have seen their playoff ambitions replaced by growing concerns over a potential relegation battle.

Norwich arrived in the South West in encouraging form, but few would have expected them to inflict such a heavy defeat on Skubala's side, with the 5-0 loss at Ashton Gate subsequently described by the manager as one of the most difficult afternoons of his career.

Although the Robins face one of the division's strongest sides this weekend, they can at least take confidence from their recent record against Boro, with the North Yorkshire outfit winless in their last nine league meetings and without a victory over Bristol City since August 2021.

Middlesbrough Championship form:.

Bristol City Championship form:.

Middlesbrough could name the same starting XI that drew with Watford almost a fortnight ago, although Hellberg may be tempted to make changes as his side look to return to winning ways.

Former Robins goalkeeper Radek Vitek is expected to retain his place between the posts, while former Bristol City players Tommy Conway, Neto Borges and Luke Ayling could all come into contention to face their old club after starting on the bench last time out.

Rokas Pusktas has suffered another injury setback after undergoing surgery on a hamstring problem and has managed just 12 minutes of football for Boro since joining from Hajduk Split in August.

Hellberg will also be without Alfie Jones, who remains sidelined with a calf injury, but could welcome the Championship's leading scorer back into the fold, with Will Lankshear looking to add to his 13 league goals, which have come at an impressive rate of one every 81 minutes.

Meanwhile, Bristol City are expected to have just one absentee for Saturday's trip north, with Noah Eile likely to miss out through illness.

Although their major injury crisis from last season is very much a thing of the past, the Robins have made several unexpected changes to their recent starting lineups, making it difficult to predict the team Skubala will select.

New goalkeeper Sam Tickle was dropped in favour of Brad Collins after just 11 appearances for his new club but could be reinstated after his replacement made several high-profile errors leading to goals during his four starts, conceding an average of 2.3 goals per game during that time.

Skubala has also alternated between a lone striker and a two-man forward partnership in recent weeks and could once again make changes as he looks to turn around his side's disappointing run of form.

Rio Cardines opted out of international duty with Trinidad and Tobago over the past fortnight after featuring in every one of the Robins' Championship matches during his debut season as a professional, and he is expected to return to the attack this weekend as he looks to build on the impressive six assists he has already provided.

Middlesbrough possible starting lineup:.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Bryam; Berhalter, Morris, McGree; Conway, Strelec, Sarmiento.

Bristol City possible starting lineup:.

Tickle; Tanner, Dickie, Eissat, Pring; Williams, Randell; Cardines, Knight, Twine; Tolaj.

With one of the division's most out-of-form sides facing a team that has been exceptionally difficult to beat on home soil, we expect the result to go Middlesbrough's way.

Although the Robins boast an impressive recent record against Boro, we expect that run to come to an end on Saturday as Hellberg's side continue their push towards the top of the Championship table.

Ben Royall (2), Ollie Rawlins (2), Zac Young and Charlie Connell scored to put Chris Simmons’ side into the quarter-finals.

Recent findings suggest that simmons noted: “It was a great result for us in what could have been a really tricky game. They are a very good side and ready to push on to step four but they didn’t take the early chances they had and we were really clinical.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

“They should have been a goal in front from a mistake by us, then within 30 seconds we were 1-0 up.

“The wet/sticky surface made it difficult for both sides who looked to play but overall I think the neutrals got their money’s worth.

“It was nice to make five changes from Saturday, get minutes into lads returning from injury and reach the quarter-finals.

“The league is our priority but everyone loves a cup run.”.

It completed a perfect week for the Bears after Saturday’s 2-0 Isthmian South East win at Margate, in which Luke Bejashvili scored both. Heath host Hastings on Saturday.

Here is Andrew Crisp’s Heath v Heath match report….

On paper this midweek trip to Southern Combination League leaders Haywards Heath Town looked a potential banana skin for Chris Simmons’ Broadbridge Heath.

The hosts may be a division below the Bears but they have made a great start to the season, five points clear at the top of the Premier Division, unbeaten at home after ten matches and having knocked cup favourites Brighton & Hove Albion out by 2-0 in an earlier round, but things don’t always work out as some may predict.

Simmons made five changes to the starting line-up that won 2-0 at Margate three days earlier, four at the back including Bailey Cotton on his way back from injury and making his first start since September and Ollie Rawlins making just his second start of the season after injury.

Broadbridge Heath got off to a great start on 3 minutes when Ben Holden received the ball on the halfway line and drove forward into the Haywards Heath half before playing the ball out wide to Ben Royall advancing down the left, and the Bears full-back cut inside and struck a low right foot shot from distance into the bottom right corner of the net.

The Bears doubled their lead on 24 minutes with Holden and Royal involved again: this time Holden, in the centre of the park, played the ball into the feet of Royall with his back to goal and closely marked, the Bears defender turned his marker and ran towards the Haywards Heath penalty area before striking a low left foot shot across the goal into the far corner.

At the other end Jack Barnes powered a header from a corner onto the top of the crossbar and Bears skipper Brad Peters reacted quickly to clear the ball off the goal-line but it was Broadbridge Heath who increased their lead on 32 minutes.

An interchange of passes ended with Luke Bejashvili playing the ball into the feet of Holden who played a first time pass to Ollie Rawlins some 25 yards out and with his back to goal and the Heath striker turned sharply to power a right foot shot into the bottom right corner giving the hosts’ keeper Charlie Roberts no chance of stopping.

Minutes later Broadbridge Heath’s Sal Marino played a defence-splitting ball to send Charlie Connell through on goal but Roberts was off his line quickly to force the player wide of goal and instead Connell played the ball back into the path of Rawlins on the edge of the “D” who blasted his shot high and wide.

A minute before the break the hosts pulled a goal back when Josh Wright crossed the ball from the right flank into the Broadbridge Heath penalty area where the ball bobbled around the six yard box before falling kindly to Charlie Meehan to tap in from close range.

Broadbridge Heath restored their three goal advantage almost immediately when a long ball was played down the left channel and chased down by Rawlins who delivered a left foot cross into the path of Zac Young, who hit a sweet left foot shot from 12 yards which was saved brilliantly by Roberts. Young pounced on the loose ball and was brought down by a clumsy challenge, and the match referee immediately pointed to the penalty spot with nobody from Haywards Heath questioning the decision and Young got up to convert the spot kick for his sixth goal of the season to make it 1-4 at the break.

Haywards Heath needed an early second half goal to get back into the game but the reverse happened 2 minutes into the restart when Broadbridge Heath goalkeeper Stan Williamson intercepted a right wing cross and threw the ball out quickly to Young in the centre of the park. He drove forward to the halfway line before playing the ball wide right to Charlie Connell, who took the ball towards the goal-line and then delivered a right wing pass across the goal to Rawlins to score from six yards.

Heath added a sixth goal on the hour mark when Rawlins received the ball wide on the right and played a long ball towards the far post where it was headed in by Connell from 8 yards to near enough secure the win for the Bears.

Simmons was able to swap his players around which included the welcome return to the side for Mason Doughty, the Heath striker with eight goals from 13 games this season has missed the last eight games through injury.

Haywards Heath added a second in time added-on when a combination of Wright and Barnes won the ball off a Bears defender and linked up well down the right channel before the ball was played inside to Barnes who finished with aplomb.

BBH: Williamson, Cotton (Thiselton 60), Royall, Marino, Peters, Salaam (Richardson 65), Bejashvili, Holden, Rawlins (Doughty 70), Connell (Hards 61), Young.

And there was no ‘cup-set’ on the day with Salisbury running out 4-0 winners.

On Tuesday nighr the boot was on the other foot as City were the team looking to avoid a shock when they went to SCFL Premier side Hassocks in round three of the Sussex Transport Senior Cup.

A professional and clinical display at the Beacon ended with Chi winning 6-0 to reach the last eight of a competition that ends with an Amex Stadium final.

Two goals apiece by Emmett Dunn, Isaac Bello and top scorer Harry Bridle secured the quarter-final spot.

It was the last of a relentless run of midweek matches that have stretched City’s small squad – and the coaching staff are looking forward to a couple of game-free Tuesdays when they can work on rest, recovery and other complications.

Killpartrick stated: “We have no complaints about the outcome at Salisbury. They’re an extremely good side, very fit and played the conditions better than us.

"We kept battling and revealed fighting spirit, which is all you can ask sometimes.

According to recent reports, "You have to take into account the difference between the two clubs. They’ve been training in Kuwait, we’ve been training at Oaklands Park – and I’m not knocking Oaklands Park, by the way!

"At Hassocks we were very, very professional. We had to be and we were because that could have been a tricky tie.

"We brought in three from our B team and another youngster and were pleased with the performance and professionalism of the whole squad.".

Meanwhile after a run of seven away games in ten matches, seventh-placed City are back at Oaklands Park this Saturday to take on 14th-placed Basingstoke in a Southern League Premier South game.

After their last home match, versus Bath City, drew more than 600, they would love another major crowd in – on the day when the city centre stages its lights switch-on just after the end of the match.

Killpartrick said: “We’ve had some really entertaining home games and will aim for another.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar announced his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.

Having enjoyed retirement for 11 years, he shocked world football by agreeing a surprise transfer to Serie C outfit Ravenna, where he was set to undertake a marketing role.

It was initially understood that he would not be making a playing return, but the Brazil legend laced up his boots on Sunday and played a part in his side's opening goal.

Ravenna's honorary vice president Ariedo Braida remarked in June that the World Cup winner would regrettably not be able to play for the club due to his age.

But it appears that went up in smoke, with Ronaldinho playing 45 minutes on his return in the league clash – despite his move being dubbed a publicity stunt by the club.

Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46.

He played the first-half of the game, playing a role in the first goal for his new side.

He helped set up Giulio Donati's opening goal of the match, and raced across the field to mob the goal scorer as he celebrated.

According to recent reports, he started the game, playing the first-half before being replaced by Matteo Maggio. Before his substitution, he embraced the fans in the stands at the interval.

The icon hinted there could be more games to come, however.

He told Sky Italia after the game: 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me.

In a recent development, 'Is this my last one? I don't know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.

'It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.'.

Ronaldinho has also become a shareholder in the club.

During his illustrious career, he won the World Cup, a Champions League, two LaLiga titles and a Serie A trophy before hanging up his boots in 2015.

He also won a string of individual accolades including the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:24.

Chelsea will be looking to return to winning ways and strengthen their top-four credentials when they take on Leeds United in Saturday afternoon’s Premier League contest at Stamford Bridge.

These two teams served up a nine-goal thriller in the EFL Cup just a couple of months ago, with the West Londoners securing a 6-3 comeback victory in the third round.

Chelsea entered the international break on a sour note with just one win and three defeats to their name in all competitions, crashing out of the EFL Cup to Liverpool and enduring two setbacks in the Premier League.

The Blues responded to a surprise 2-0 home loss to Spurs by beating Man United at Stamford Bridge by the same scoreline, but they came back down to earth a fortnight ago with a disappointing 1-0 defeat to basement club Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Five wins, one draw and four defeats have been posted in Xabi Alonso’s first 10 top-flight games for Chelsea, who sit fifth in the Premier League table and just two points behind Liverpool in fourth. However, Aston Villa down in 10th spot are only three points adrift of the Blues.

Having lost three of their first five PL away games for the first time since 2015-16 under Jose Mourinho, Chelsea should welcome this weekend’s return to Stamford Bridge where they have accumulated 10 of their 16 top-flight points this term, scoring the second-most home goals in the division (13).

The West Londoners have also won eight of their last 10 home battles with Leeds across all tournaments (D2) since a 2-0 defeat back in December 1999, though they were held to a 2-2 draw in this exact league fixture last season after letting a two-goal lead slip in the second half.

Following a five-match winless run that placed Daniel Farke under growing pressure, Leeds secured a much-needed 1-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road to enter the international break on a high.

A dominant second-half display was rewarded with a late strike from substitute Noah Okafor to help Leeds claim their third Premier League win of the season and rise to ninth in the table, six points clear of the bottom three and just two points behind Saturday’s opponents Chelsea in fifth.

Leeds are unbeaten across their last nine Premier League home matches (W5 D4) – their longest run at Elland Road in the top flight since an impressive 15-match streak between January and December 2001 – but they have only won one of their last eight league games on the road (D4 L3).

The Whites are now gearing up for four tricky away trips to Chelsea, Man City, Liverpool and Aston Villa, with Farke hoping that his side can showcase the same relentless character, commitment and unity shown in their win over Spurs as they attempt to improve their fortunes away from home.

According to recent reports, leeds head into this weekend’s contest seeking to end a 10-game winless run away against Chelsea in all competitions (D2 L8). However, having avoided defeat in their last two league meetings (3-1 at home, 2-2 away), the Whites will aim to go three consecutive games unbeaten against the Blues for the first time since between November 2000 and October 2001.

Chelsea form (all competitions):.

Leeds United Premier League form:.

Chelsea’s Reece James (knee), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) all remain sidelined with injuries, but there is hope that Joao Pedro could be ready to return after missing the last four matches with a thigh problem.

Moises Caicedo (illness), Jorrel Hato (back) and Josh Acheampong (unspecified) are all doubtful, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez should be ready to start ahead for Mike Penders after recovering from a broken jaw to represent Argentina during the international break.

In a recent development, morgan Rogers provided four second-half assists in the aforementioned EFL Cup win over Leeds in September, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both netted a brace. However, Welbeck may have to settle for a place on the bench once again, with Alonso possibly favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central role alongside Rogers and Palmer.

As for Leeds, young forward Mateo Joseph is making positive progress in his recovery from a serious knee injury, but he remains sidelined, while midfielder Anton Stach is doubtful after missing the win over Spurs with a broken toe.

Farke will consider sticking with a two-man frontline of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, with Sean Longstaff and Ao Tanaka linking up with ex-Chelsea youngster Ethan Ampadu in midfield.

However, Noah Okafor will hope to force his way into the first XI after scoring as a substitute against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are also contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom recently recovered from a long-term injury.

Chelsea possible starting lineup:.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Palestra; Estevao, Rogers, Palmer.

Leeds United possible starting lineup:.

Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Tanaka, Ampadu, Gudmundsson; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin.

Chelsea have not been the same prolific outfit without the presence of Joao Pedro up front, and they could find it difficult to break down a robust Leeds backline without a natural focal point.

Despite only one of the Blues' last six Premier League matches seeing both teams score, we can see the net rippling at both ends on this occasion, with the hosts bouncing back from recent setbacks and edging to a slender victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Industry observers note that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

Recent findings suggest that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

It has been revealed that equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

It has been revealed that carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

Sources indicate that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

According to recent reports, “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager mentioned. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

According to recent reports, it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

It has been revealed that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

According to recent reports, united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Recent findings suggest that it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and promptly.

Industry observers note that speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick mentioned: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

It has been revealed that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

Recent findings suggest that “We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

Industry observers note that “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

Spool forward 12 years, and United had a chance at restoring their good name in West Sussex, again in the Senior Cup.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After a deluge on the way to the game, the United faithful were pleasantly surprised to see a pleasant evening for this step 4 v step 5 encounter.

As the referee got the match underway, it became immediately obvious that Anthony Storey’s boys were giving no quarter at all to the higher league team – Joe Overy running head down at the defence time and again as Charlie Ball, Callum Barlow and James Hull all went close top opening the scoring, with no real penetration from Bognor until the 20th minute, when Zach Robitaille and Dan Hull combined to clear off the line.

According to recent reports, on the half hour, Overy decided to go it alone, his shot going just over the bar. Jorge Nones was looking very lively indeed and was unfortunate not to score, the Bognor keeper again earning his corn with a point blank save.

As the teams went in 0-0 at half time, nerves were showing among the Bognor crowd – maybe the lower league team will run out of steam?

Had they done their homework, they would know that Eastbourne United are one of the fittest teams in the SCFL Premier, and so it was that as the teams came out for the second half, if anything United had stepped their game up.

In a recent development, james Hull had picked up a nasty cut in the first half and was replaced by the lively Freddie Jones on the hour. Almost straight away, Overy crossed for Barlow who made no mistake against his old club, to the absolute horror of the home support.

Bognor made a triple change in response, but to be honest did not really look to have an answer. James Stone replaced Barlow a few minutes later, and within minutes Ball broke down the right, his cross finding Stone for a great finish and 2-0. The upset was definitely on the cards.

Recent findings suggest that alieu Secka saved well from Cal Laycock, but with 5 minutes to go, the lifeline appeared and it was 2-1. United were not rattled – quite the opposite as Jones went straight up the other end and crossed for Overy to make it 3-1.

According to recent reports, alfie Gander replaced Ball as the game moved to 6 minutes of added time. Right at the end Bognor snuck a second goal, but it was too late, it made for an exciting last couple of minutes, but everyone knew that the game was up, indeed as the referee blew the final whistle there was generous applause from the Rocks supporters after a game played in a very good atmosphere.

Eastbourne United are in the quarter-finals and ready for another adventure in the next round.

On Saturday Guernsey are the visitors to the Oval for a 2pm kick-off, another match that will be vital in United’s promotion push.

Industry observers note that eastbourne Town’s Senior Cup interest is over. Sonny Walsh’s goal wasn’t enough to prevent a 2-1 defeat to Lewes at The Saffrons, also on Tuesday night.

Recent findings suggest that but there was better news for Jude Macdonald’s team in the Isthmian South East last Saturday – they drew 1-1 at Sheppey, with Alfie Rogers their scorer. That ended a run of eight league defeats on the trot for Town and took them off bottom spot, now occupied by Horley.

Macdonald’s men host Whitstable tomorrow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Premier League and EFL are set to hold serious conversations about the blackout’s future next year with pretty much every TV slot now exhausted.

Removing the blackout – which is a rule that prevents live football matches from being broadcast on television or streaming services between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays – could have a detrimental effect on attendances and finances, especially clubs in the lower tiers like Crawley Town.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The blackout is under threat and television rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and Scottish Premiership are all up for renewal in 2029-30 and last year, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters noted there were no prepares to remove the blackout – introduced in 2003 by UEFA as Article 48.

According to recent reports, but this summer there appeared to be a shift in emphasis, with Masters saying there would be talks with the EFL ahead of the renewal of TV rights. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged caution and suggested the health of the football pyramid should come first.

The only leagues that apply Article 48 are England, Scotland and Northern Ireland. No other major country qualifies for the blackout - it is a tradition that is unique to football in the United Kingdom.

But how would it affect Crawley Town?

CEO Allman gave his personal opinion – and not necessarily that of the club – about the situation and what it would mean if it ended.

It has been revealed that he said: “My personal opinion is that the 3pm blackout presently works well in protecting the current football pyramid. I hear the arguments about it not being in place in other countries, but there is no pyramid like the UK pyramid so am not sure it is a fair comparison.

"We see notable increases in attendances during international breaks as well as drop offs for Tuesday night games for example where they are available on SkySports+ so in general, whilst removing the blackout, would arguably increase the exposure of clubs like Crawley, would levy that with actual attendances dropping off, which whilst having the obvious financial implication, will also have impacts on atmospheres and the general match-day feel.”.

So it’s clear whether he would oppose the ending of the blackout? “I wouldn’t be in favour - as I say, I think the pyramid is what stands us apart from other countries and sports, and with that, would encourage fans to go out and experience the full pyramid, rather than looking for more Premier League games on TV.”.

He added: “Whilst I understand the argument of increased coverage, I wouldn’t levy that against supporters being in the stadium, buying a pint, eating a burger, cheering their team on and in turn, financially supporting the club to allow us to kick on across the board.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Rangers and Sunderland head coach Michael Beale has broken his silence on his turbulent 177-day spell in charge of Belgian Pro League side Zulte Waregem after resigning last week.

Beale, 46, brought down the curtain on his short time at the Elindus Arena following the 4-1 defeat to Sint-Truidense last week, which made it six consecutive league defeats. Their worst run of results since October 7, 2018, they are just four points above the relegation zone.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Industry observers note that his spell in Belgium was plagued by rumours of a breakdown in his relationship with senior figures at the club over Waregem’s direction and strategy. Beale actually started the campaign brightly, going unbeaten in their opening five games. However, their form promptly deteriorated, and they have failed to register a victory since September 6.

His first managerial role since being sacked after just 12 games in charge at Sunderland almost three years ago, he exited Waregem with an identical record to the one he held at the Stadium of Light, with four wins, two draws, and six losses, meaning he left both sides with a 33.3% win rate after 12 games.

In a short statement confirming his departure, Waregem noted: “After several internal discussions between the head coach and the club, both parties decided to end their collaboration by mutual agreement.” Zulte Waregem are yet to appoint Beale’s permanent successor, with interim head coach Steve Colpaert expected to take charge of their league game vs Royal Antwerp at the weekend.

A week on from his departure, Beale penned an emotional farewell message to Waregem via his official Instagram page, writing: “Waregem, thankyou. It has been an honour and privilege to manage this club and I want to begin by thanking the fans for their incredible support. From day one, your passion and loyalty stood out and made coaching this club feel truly special. I will never forget the welcome you gave me and I have been overwhelmed by all your messages and kind words over the last few days.

“This community has become a home to me and to everyone I met in the local shops, coffee houses, parks, restaurants and bars: thank you. Many of you have become true friends and you have made me feel completely one of your own. I also want to show my gratitude to the players and staff for their hard work, dedication and the special memories we created together. You have been a pleasure to work with and I wish you every success in the future.”.

Recent findings suggest that the ex-Rangers manager first joined Rangers as first-team coach during Steven Gerrard’s spell as manager at Ibrox. However, he left to join the former Liverpool icon in a similar role when he was appointed at Aston Villa in November 2021. Shortly afterwards, Beale took on his first managerial role with Queens Park Rangers.

He lasted just six months at Loftus Road before being poached by Rangers as a replacement for Giovanni van Bronckhorst. He struggled in the main role at Rangers, though, and was sacked in October 2023 before joining Sunderland three months later.

#2120. More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has major aims for AC Milan.
  • The RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment.
  • Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has major aims for AC Milan.

The RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment. Of course AC Milan will be at the centre of the web, but the idea is to expand.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that the proof of this comes from a three-letter acronym: MSE. It stands for Milan Sports & Entertainment and it is the upcoming holding company created by RedBird. The idea, simply put, is to bring together investments and activities in various sectors under one umbrella.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport recall, Cardinale explained to the Financial Times that the assets involved could be valued in the mid-single-digit billions, meaning several billion dollars. So, how does he initiative to get there?

Cardinale linked the creation of MSE to the process initiated with the acquisition of Milan: “Milan Sports & Entertainment is the culmination of this work and of what we have built since we first invested in the club four years ago.”.

In his interview with La Gazzetta, Cardinale clarified that the new structure is also created to support the Rossoneri’s sporting ambitions: “The driving force behind operations like this is to provide Milan with the financial strength needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.”.

In a recent development, there are examples of this kind of model working already. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, AEG and Fenway Sports Group are among the most prominent and – given his background in the USA – Cardinale knows each of them well.

According to CNBC valuations, KSE was worth $26.05bn in 2026, FSG $15.37bn, and AEG $11.99bn in 2025, excluding music and hotel businesses.

According to recent reports, KSE boasts franchises such as the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal, as well as venues such as SoFi Stadium, Ball Arena, and Emirates Stadium. The group combines sports, infrastructure and real estate development such as Hollywood Park, the district built around SoFi Stadium.

AEG – founded by Philip Anschutz – have instead built its model on the management and development of venues. It owns or manages venues such as Crypto.com Arena and The O2 in London plus the Los Angeles Kings and LA Galaxy, and operates in concert promotion and ticketing. The LA LIVE project developed around Crypto.com Arena puts the venue at the centre of a greater ecosystem.

Industry observers note that fenway Sports Group – born around the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool FC – have developed a holding company with interests in media, marketing, real estate, and entertainment. It’s a model Cardinale knows first hand: in 2021, RedBird invested approximately $750m in FSG, acquiring a stake of around 11%, based on an enterprise valuation of $7.35bn.

Industry observers note that MSE in theory can harness elements of all three of these experiences: KSE’s integration of sports and infrastructure, AEG ‘s commercial development of facilities and FSG ‘s multi-sport approach. The main difference is the purpose declared by Cardinale: to use all of it to funnel money back into Milan.

From the stadium shared with Inter to the possibility of an arena in San Donato, including the upcoming NBA Europe venture and even tennis: MSE’s scope includes various initiatives that go beyond the playing field.

The main infrastructure project is the future Generali Stadium, the newly introduced 71,500-seat facility designed by Foster + Partners and Manica. Developed jointly by the two Milanese clubs, it represents a key element of the transformation of the San Siro area and will not be a Rossoneri-only facility.

Industry observers note that the promoters intend for the stadium to host year-round activities, from matches to concerts, as well as catering, events, and hospitality services. In other words, like the stadiums and arenas mentioned above, it will become more than just a place to go for two hours on a Sunday.

In San Donato Milanese, RedBird are also considering the possibility of building a 20,000-seat arena. Cardinale explained that the fund already owns the land and has planning permission, but the idea is also linked to Milan’s potential involvement in NBA Europe. Another area of ​​focus concerns tennis, with the possibility of hosting a tournament in the city.

According to recent reports, finally, RedBird intend to develop a company dedicated to managing stadiums and arenas, with services including catering, merchandising and premium hospitality. The goal is to build commercial expertise to apply to the facilities connected to the group, but also to make it available to other owners and sports clubs.

Recent findings suggest that this phase will be co-ordinated by Brett Yormark, appointed CEO of MSE and set to step down as head of the Substantial 12 (a conference in College Football) at the end of January 2027. He worked for 14 years at Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, overseeing the development of the Brooklyn Nets and the Barclays Center. He has also gained experience in NASCAR and Roc Nation.

The choice to go for Yormark reflects the desire to entrust the platform to someone with expertise across multiple different fields in the sporting and commercial worlds.

All these grand prepares are well and good, but how will ideas turn into money that drives AC Milan forward? MSE’s economic potential is measured not only through the club’s revenues, but also through the activities that RedBird intends to develop around sports, infrastructure and entertainment.

The starting point is obviously Milan as a club, which closed the 2025-26 financial year with revenues of €464.6m, over €100m of which came from sponsorships. The main infrastructure opportunity is the upcoming San Siro, an investment of approximately €2.3bn shared with Inter.

Projections contained in the design documents indicate a potential annual revenue of approximately €120.4m for the facility as a whole (both for the Rossoneri and the Nerazzurri), through sporting, commercial, and complementary services.

In a recent development, these are numbers that will be revised upwards by the two clubs when considering, for example, the record agreement with Generali for naming rights. It is worth a total of €650m over 25 years, divided into €10m per year for the first five years and €30m per season for the following 20, once the stadium is built.

One of the areas on which RedBird Capital are focusing most is hospitality, which is right now worth around €15m per year for the Rossoneri. The international benchmark has already been set by Legends Global, a tech giant Cardinale knows well.

According to recent reports, legends are what the Milan owner sees as a model for developing premium services, restaurants, and commercial spaces. The most obvious example is at FC Barcelona: with the support of LG, the club have marketed nearly 5,000 VIP seats at Camp Nou, generating over €380m in contracted revenue.

They aim to generate another €700m through multi-year licenses for an additional 2,000 seats. This isn’t annual revenue, but rather contracts spread over 15 or 30 years, so a guaranteed flow of money coming in that Cardinale aims to replicate.

It has been revealed that another agreement which demonstrates the potential of this kind of arrangement is the one with Real Madrid for the Santiago Bernabéu. It involves an investment of approximately €360m in exchange for 20-year participation in some of the stadium’s businesses,.

Legends Global also operate in facilities and events management. Following the acquisition of ASM Global (who actually proposed renovating San Siro for non-football events in Italy) in 2024, the group claims a presence in over 450 venues, approximately 20,000 events, and 165 million guests annually. Their European partnerships include Arsenal, Chelsea and Porto.

FC Barcelona introduces new VIP seating licenses at Spotify Camp Nou with Legends Global.

🔗 More details: https://t.co/awtEsnYE6X pic.twitter.com/iCMuM0QD35.

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 25, 2026.

It has been revealed that to illustrate the potential it could hold for Italy as a whole, the English subsidiary reported revenues of £131.6m in 2024, of which £105.5m came from facility and event management and £26.1m from catering. Before the integration with ASM Global, Legends had reported revenues of $1.7bn in the period ending in March 2024, with 67% coming from food and beverage sales.

In a recent development, in Italy, a benchmark is Forumnet, who in 2024 generated €29.7m in revenue and €12.8m in EBITDA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation). They manage the Assago Forum which hosts approximately 60-70 concerts a year, demonstrating how a venue can generate activity well beyond the sports calendar.

As mentioned, an arena is being planned in San Donato with an estimated investment of around €400m, which could become the basis for a Milanese franchise in NBA Europe. For reference, Olimpia Milano – the current basketball team in the city – generate around €15m through ticketing, season tickets, sponsorships and merchandising.

According to recent reports, for NBA Europe, projections speak of over $1.5bn to be distributed to the clubs in the first six years. A theoretical division among the 12 permanent franchises would equate to approximately $20.8m per team per year, but this is not fixed yet. Entry costs – estimated by the media to be between $500m and over $1bn – also remain to be determined.

Tennis represents another potential area for development. The ATP 500 in Halle generates around €5m in revenue, excluding television rights, while the ATP Finals in Turin generate around €60m. These are events with different dimensions and scopes, but they provide a scale.

The creation of MSE has a stated objective: to strengthen Milan’s financial capacity and reduce the gap with the richest clubs on the international scene, particularly those in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that the gap is also evident when comparing revenues. AC Milan closed the 2025-26 season with €464.6m, a significant result considering their absence from European competitions , but still far from the top English clubs.

Recent findings suggest that according to the Deloitte Football Money League, in the 2024-25 season, Liverpool generated €836.1m, Arsenal €821.7m and Manchester United €793.1m. Tottenham and Chelsea also exceeded €670m and €580m, respectively.

The comparison covers different financial years, but it still shows the magnitude of the gap. Liverpool generated revenues equal to approximately 1.8 times those of Milan, while Chelsea recorded a turnover approximately €120 higher.

The chasm demonstrates how clubs in the Premier League have showcased an ability to generate commercial revenue, enhance stadiums and reach a global audience. The gap has only been growing, and TV rights will be another focus, though that is outside of just Cardinale’s hands.

Industry observers note that speaking of the owner, it is now obvious he sees MSE as the name that will house the tools to try build a real sporting and commercial world around Milan. It remains to be seen how effective it will be, but the starting point is there.

  • Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.
  • The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 16:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:37.

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lille head into the weekend in encouraging form after winning their last two league outings, beating Lens 1-0 before claiming a 2-1 victory away to Rennes prior to the international break, where Nathan Ngoy's second-half goal proved decisive.

Davide Ancelotti will be particularly pleased with how his side have rediscovered their rhythm after consecutive draws against Brest and Monaco derailed the Mastiffs' title charge, with the northern French outfit having lost just once in their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (W6, D3).

Much of Lille's success this season has been built on their defensive solidity, with seven goals conceded representing the best record in the division, while five clean sheets leave them behind only Lorient (six) in that regard.

Les Dogues have also found the net in every league outing this season, although they have scored more than once in just 40% of their 10 top-flight matches, including two of their five fixtures on their own turf.

Nevertheless, Lille have been reliable at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, winning three of their five Ligue 1 games at the ground and avoiding defeat in the other two to boast the division's fifth-best home record.

Victory on Saturday would not only strengthen the hosts' position in the standings but also provide a timely confidence boost ahead of Wednesday's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich, with the Mastiffs currently second from bottom in the league phase table after collecting just one point from their opening four continental fixtures.

Vicens will also have one eye on next Thursday’s home meeting with Lillstrom in the Europa League, where Lyon sit 13th in the 36-team table after picking up seven points from their first four matches.

However, the Spanish coach's immediate priority will be to get his fresh side back to winning ways following a 2-0 defeat at Brest in Lyon's most recent league outing, which came under interim boss Jorge Maciel following the departure of Paolo Fonseca for Sporting Lisbon.

That setback further highlighted Lyon's struggles on the road, having now lost their last three Ligue 1 away matches while conceding exactly two goals in each of those outings, with their only victory in five domestic trips this season coming against Toulouse on the opening weekend.

Nevertheless, a superior head-to-head record should offer the visitors some encouragement ahead of Saturday's contest, considering Lyon have won six of their last seven meetings across all competitions (D1) with Lille, including 1-0 victories in both league encounters last season.

Lille remain without Tiago Santos, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after rupturing his cruciate ligament, while Hamza Igamane is also unavailable as he continues his recovery from an ACL injury, although a return is expected in December.

Ayase Ueda is doubtful after sustaining a plantar fascia injury, with the forward having resumed running but yet to return to full training, although Ancelotti previously suggested that the Japanese attacker could be available for this fixture.

Hakon Arnar Haraldsson has operated as a makeshift centre-forward in Ueda's absence and could continue in that position if the latter fails to recover in time, although veteran striker Olivier Giroud also provides an alternative.

Meanwhile, Lyon will be without Tyler Morton, who recently underwent surgery for an abductor problem, while Pavel Sulc is recovering from a meniscus injury and Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for the remainder of the campaign after rupturing his cruciate ligament.

Lois Openda also remains unavailable as he recovers from a fractured fibula, although the forward is expected to return in the coming weeks, while Steeve Kango could be available after rejoining group training following a period under concussion protocol.

Lille possible starting lineup:.

Ozer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Perraud; Bentaleb, Andre, Mukau; E Mbappe, Haraldsson, Diaoune.

Greif; Athekame, Niakhate, Bacher, A Vinicius; Tessmann, Bidstrup, Tolisso; Nuamah, Merah, Nakamura.

Lyon's recent dominance in this fixture makes the visitors difficult to dismiss, particularly with Vicens hoping to make an immediate impression in his first match at the helm.

However, Lille's superior defensive record, unbeaten home form and greater consistency in the league should give Ancelotti's side the edge, and we expect the hosts to secure a narrow victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On a damp evening on the Sussex coast, Lewes defeated Step 4 Town 2-1 to make the last eight.

Two goals of varying difficulty from Bassett laid the foundations for the win, with the Rooks then withstanding Town’s pressure after a Sonny Walsh strike to make progress.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

While it was not the most fluent outing for Lewes, several performances on an evening of experimentation will give reason for optimism.

The Rooks arrived at The Saffrons with six changes to their starting XI, including Josh Spinks’ return as captain and a debut for upcoming attacking signing Kwesi Ntim.

Ntim, who has scored 20 goals in 33 games for Lingfield in 2026, was a bright spark early on, cutting in from the left flank and posing problems for the home defence.

Genuine chances took a while to arrive on the south coast, with the opening stages dominated by safe possession football.

After 25 minutes, however, Lewes created their first threat as Bassett worked space on the right and forced goalkeeper Chris Winterton to punch a cross into the path of Brian Garzon, whose right-footed effort was cleared off the line.

The Rooks slowly built the pressure from here, with Tyler Christian-Law and Mackenzie Richardson driving at goal before the opener soon arrived.

Industry observers note that in the 37th minute, Ntim added a flash of brilliance with a pacey drive in from the left, setting up Richardson for a first-time effort at goal. With ex-Rooks ‘keeper Winterton spilling the ball, Bassett was on hand to tap home.

Richardson had another bite at a goal of his own before the break, but Winterton stood up well to a rising effort from the left of the box to keep the score at 0-1.

Lewes did not hesitate in doubling down on their advantage at the start of the second half, and Bassett was the man to deliver again.

Barely 30 seconds into the half, the forward stormed down the right and cut into the box before producing an audacious chip on Winterton that dropped into the top left corner.

It was a moment of magic, and whether Bassett had meant it or not, nobody could begrudge the striker his fourth goal of the season thus far.

The Rooks got into a rhythm after this, regularly wriggling free of Town's attentions and finding space on the counter without truly putting the game to bed.

Bassett and Ntim were similarly denied in the area, while Garzon had at least two notable chances while cutting inside that flew inches wide of the post.

All the while, Town were never out of the tie, and they got their spark in the 61st minute.

Sonny Walsh was set free on the right of the box and blasted an effort past Louis Rogers to halve the deficit.

Town had two brilliant chances to level the scores in the final 30 minutes, but as has been their story in the last few weeks, luck was against them.

A ball in from the right was stabbed over the crossbar from close range, and in the dying stages, Walsh was again set free on the right but blasted over the target.

Equally, Lewes could have added to their advantage as substitute Omar Al-Seadi prodded wide of the left post when excellently teed up by a combination of Bassett and Kurtis Cumberbatch.

Altogether, Lewes were relieved to hear the final whistle as they made it to the final eight, but were good value for the result across the 90 minutes.

At the time of writing, the timing of the draw for the Quarter-Finals, and the dates of this round, are yet to be declared.

We anticipate news of both in due course, and urge supporters to keep tabs on our social media pages for the latest updates.

This Saturday, the Rooks are back in Isthmian Premier Division action away at Ramsgate FC.

Sources indicate that with Lewes in 5th and Ramsgate - with a game in hand - just three points behind in 6th, it has all the makings of an excellent game at Southwood Stadium. Kick-off is at 3pm.

Lewes FC: Rogers; Mundele, Spinks (C), Hamstead, Cox (Allen, 69’); Christian-Law, Garzon, Richardson (Unwin, 76’); Fisher (Cumberbatch, 85’), Bassett (Mahmoud, 90’), Ntim (Al-Seadi, 69’).
